newsitem.title: USA: Moody's warns of effect of Calif. tax measure.
newsitem.headline: Moody's warns of effect of Calif. tax measure.

text.p: The credit ratings of some local governments in California could be undermined by a controversial tax measure approved by voters earlier this month, Moody's Investors Service Inc warned Friday.

Proposition 218 would strengthen existing law to require that new local taxes be submitted to voters for approval. It would also allow property owners to approve new assessments and strictly limit the use of fees and charges.
"The breadth of the amendment's provisions raises numerous credit concerns and, eventually, many ratings are likely to be negatively affected," Moody's said in a report.

"It is impossible to determine at this time, however, which specific ratings will be affected," Moody's said. "The full impact of the new fiscal restrictions will not manifest itself for years, most likely during a future recession."

Moody's said many cities and counties in the state will face new budget pressures as a result of the measure. This pressure will hurt the credit quality of debt tied to general funds, the rating agency said.
Fees and charges backing water, sewer and solid waste debt will be subject to new approval procedures. The change may keep some issuers from meeting rate covenants, Moody's said.
Since school district funding options were already limited, most districts in the state should be relatively unaffected by Proposition 218's passage, Moody's said.
The handful of schools that have imposed landscaping assessments, however, may find a new hole in their revenue structures, the rating agency warned.
"But the measure's complexity and ambiguity make it difficult to reach firm conclusions so soon after its passage," Moody's concluded.
